html:
Unfinished novel by the Marquis de Sade, written in secret in the Bastille prison in Paris in 1785. It describes four rich men who lock themselves away to indulge in cruelty, and is among the most extreme books ever written.

Sade wrote it in tiny script on a paper roll about twelve metres long, in about 37 days in autumn 1785, and hid it in his cell wall. Only the first part was finished, and the rest was notes.

In July 1789, days before the crowd stormed the Bastille during the French Revolution, Sade was moved out, shouting to passers-by that prisoners were being killed. He lost the roll in the move and said he wept over it. Someone had found it, and it passed through collectors until published in 1904 by a German doctor, Iwan Bloch.

The book gave "sadism" part of its meaning and was banned for much of the 1900s.
